title: Arbitrary algebraic-space thickenings remain thickenings under base change
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable map whose every base change to a scheme is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Give the point spaces their quotient topology from surjective etale scheme atlases [def-a1-space-point-topology], with field-valued point classes as in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Let $i:Z\to W$ be a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism $|Z|\to|W|$; such a map is called a thickening. Then $i$ is a monomorphism (for every algebraic space $H$ and maps $a,b:H\to Z$, $ia=ib$ implies $a=b$). For every morphism $T\to W$ of algebraic spaces, the projection $Z\times_WT\to T$ is again a thickening, and in particular induces a homeomorphism on point spaces. There is no finite order or finite type assumption.

source.place: Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening); monomorphism assertion: spaces-morphisms.tex, Tag 042R (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms), applied to a closed immersion.

proof.text: First consider any representable closed immersion $j:E\to F$ of algebraic spaces, without assuming surjectivity. Fix a scheme $R$ and two sections $e_1,e_2\in E(R)$ with common image $c\in F(R)$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], the sheaf $P=h_R\times_FE$ is represented by a scheme; its projection $q:P\to R$ is a closed immersion by the hypothesis on $j$. The sections $(\operatorname{id}_R,e_1)$ and $(\operatorname{id}_R,e_2)$ give two scheme sections of $q$. By the forward implication of [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed], $q$ is a monomorphism, so these sections agree and $e_1=e_2$. Thus $E(R)\to F(R)$ is injective for every $R$. For algebraic-space maps $a,b:H\to E$ with $ja=jb$, evaluate on every $h\in H(R)$ and apply this injectivity; every component of $a$ equals that of $b$, so the natural transformations agree. Apply this to $i$.

source.place: Tag 042R (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms), with scheme monomorphism supplied by etale.tex Tag 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion), (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Fix $t:T\to W$ and form $P=Z\times_WT$ with projection $p:P\to T$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every scheme $R\to T$, the universal property identifies $P\times_TR$ with $Z\times_WR$, compatibly with projection to $R$: on sections, $((z,u),r)$ corresponds to $(z,r)$ with $u$ the image of $r$. Because $i$ is representable and a closed immersion on all scheme tests, $Z\times_WR$ is a scheme closed in $R$. Consequently $p$ is a representable closed immersion. Step 1, which was proved for every such immersion, also makes $p$ a monomorphism and makes its maps on scheme sections injective.

source.place: Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening), closed-immersion clause, verified directly on scheme tests.

proof.text: The homeomorphism hypothesis on $i$ makes $|i|$ surjective. For any point $x\in|T|$, choose a representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$. Choose a point of $Z$ above its image in $|W|$, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$. By [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], there is a common field extension $M$ on which their maps to $W$ agree. The resulting pair is a section of the sheaf fibre product $P$ over $\operatorname{Spec}M$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], giving a point above $x$. Hence $|p|$ is surjective. If two point classes of $P$ have the same image in $|T|$, the same point-class definition gives a common field extension on which their images as sections of $T$ agree. Injectivity on scheme sections from step 2 then makes their sections of $P$ agree. Thus their point classes agree, proving that $|p|$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), explicit common-field proof; injectivity is the same point-class argument with the monomorphism from step 2.

proof.text: For every scheme $R\to T$, step 2 makes $P\times_TR\to R$ a closed immersion of schemes. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Thus $p$ is finite on scheme tests, exactly the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology]. That node gives continuity and closedness of $|p|$ for the atlas topologies. A continuous closed bijection is a homeomorphism: if $C\subseteq|P|$ is closed, its inverse image under the inverse bijection is $|p|(C)$, which is closed. Together with step 2, this proves that $p$ is a thickening. No step used finite order, finite type, or any nilpotence bound.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-b9b37b8af (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full against the base item (unsplit, empty proof in live and side-live; no repair note, so not a re-split). The statement is unchanged apart from added citations to def-a1-space-point-topology and def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes. Source: Stacks 09ZX (proof omitted; only the thickening clause is claimed, not first/finite order), definition-thickening, 042R, and 03H4/section-points in spaces-properties.tex, all read. Step 1: the scheme test P=h_R×_F E is a closed immersion, which is a monomorphism by the Mathlib leaf lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed; two sections of q are therefore equal, giving componentwise cancellation. Step 2: (Z×_W T)×_T R = Z×_W R through the scheme test R→T→W, so p is a representable closed immersion and, by step 1, a monomorphism. Step 3: surjectivity is the common-field argument of 03H4; injectivity uses the restrictions to a common field M and injectivity of P(M)→T(M). This needs transitivity of the point relation, which is elementary and holds for any presheaf by amalgamating field extensions. Step 4: closed immersions are finite (Mathlib leaf), which is exactly the hypothesis of lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology; it gives continuity and closedness, and a continuous closed bijection is a homeomorphism. Edge cases checked: identity, empty T, the nil but not nilpotent thickening Spec k → Spec k[x_n]/(x_n^{n+1}), and a non-surjective closed immersion, which fails only the surjectivity half of step 3. The parent's universal-homeomorphism use is covered. No algebraic-space duplicate exists (only scheme-level 09ZU analogues) and there is no cycle. The tool_use lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers (generic fibre products) is accepted. Batch-5: def-a1-space-point-topology and def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes are general definitions, and lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology is a generic topology lemma for finite maps of spaces. All three reach sec-trace-formula only through the definition def-trf-algebraic-space, with no trace-formula, Poincaré or nt-assume node in their closure, so they lie outside the assumptions and are accepted. No SGA source. No fixes.
